questions.question: Anantha R Krishnan is associated with which musical instrument?
questions.questionHtml: Anantha R Krishnan is associated with which musical instrument?
questions.solution: Anantha R Krishnan is a renowned musician associated with the Mridangam, a classical percussion instrument from South India used in Carnatic music. The Mridangam is a double-headed drum, producing both bass and treble sounds. Celebrated for his skill and innovative techniques, Anantha R Krishnan has significantly contributed to the instrument's prominence in classical music. The Mridangam, traditionally made from jackfruit wood with animal skin heads, is vital in Carnatic concerts and Bharatanatyam dance performances. Modern players, including Krishnan, have expanded its versatility by incorporating contemporary techniques.

questions.question: U Srinivas is associated with which musical instrument?
questions.questionHtml: U Srinivas is associated with which musical instrument?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Mandolin.

Key Points

  • U Srinivas was a renowned Indian mandolin player in the Carnatic classical music tradition.
  • He is widely recognized for bringing the mandolin to the forefront of Indian classical music.
  • He started learning music at a very young age and gave his first public performance at the age of 9.
  • U Srinivas received numerous awards including the Padma Shri and Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for his contributions to music.

Additional Information

  • Mandolin:
    • The mandolin is a stringed musical instrument in the lute family and is usually plucked with a plectrum or pick.
    • It commonly has four courses of doubled metal strings tuned in unison, although there are many variations.
    • Mandolins are used in a variety of musical genres including classical, folk, bluegrass, and rock.
    • In Indian classical music, particularly Carnatic music, the mandolin has been adapted and popularized by musicians like U Srinivas.
  • Carnatic Music:
    • Carnatic music is a system of music commonly associated with southern India, and it is one of the two main subgenres of Indian classical music.
    • It emphasizes a highly structured rhythmic and melodic framework and is known for its complex compositions and improvisational aspects.
    • Instruments commonly used in Carnatic music include the veena, mridangam, violin, and mandolin.
    • U Srinivas's adaptation of the mandolin to Carnatic music has inspired many young musicians to take up the instrument.
  • Padma Shri:
    • Padma Shri is the fourth highest civilian award in the Republic of India.
    • It is awarded to citizens of India in recognition of their distinguished contribution in various spheres including arts, education, industry, literature, science, sports, medicine, social service, and public affairs.
    • U Srinivas was awarded the Padma Shri in 1998 for his contributions to Indian classical music.
  • Sangeet Natak Akademi Award:
    • The Sangeet Natak Akademi Award is an award given by the Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's National Academy of Music, Dance & Drama.
    • It is the highest Indian recognition given to practicing artists.
    • U Srinivas received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 2010 for his exceptional contribution to Carnatic music.

questions.question: Who among the following has been credited with developing a notation system for Indian classical music?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following has been credited with developing a notation system for Indian classical music?
questions.solution: Vishnu Narayan Bhatkhande is credited with developing a widely used notation system for Indian classical music, which helped transcribe and standardize it. He extensively traveled across India to document and classify compositions, laying the foundation for modern music education in the country. Bhatkhande established several music colleges and institutions, making Indian classical music more accessible. His pioneering work in musicology includes publishing several books on the subject, earning him the title "Father of Modern Hindustani Music". Other notable figures in Indian classical music mentioned include Kumar Gandharva, Bal Gandharva, and Bhimsen Joshi.

questions.question: Pandit Ram Narayan was a popular __________ player who is credited with making the instrument as a solo concert instrument.
questions.questionHtml: Pandit Ram Narayan was a popular __________ player who is credited with making the instrument as a solo concert instrument.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Sarangi.

Key Points​

  • The sarangi is a bowed instrument that was made popular by Indian artist Pandit Ram Narayan as a solo performance instrument in Hindustani classical music.
  • He also became the first sarangi performer to achieve fame on a global scale.
  • The sarangi is played with a bow just like a violin, but in contrast to the violin, it is held vertically with the sound chamber below.
  • It normally has three primary strings, with a fourth string serving as a drone occasionally.
  • A solo concerto is a type of music in which an orchestra plays behind a single solo instrument that plays the melodic line.
  • A solo concerto has three movements: a quick section, a slow section, and then another fast section.

 Additional Information​

  • Mridangam:
    • The two-headed drum known as the mridangam, it is used in southern Indian Karnatak music.
    • It has an outline resembling an extended hexagon and is made of wood in the form of an angular barrel. India's top-ranked mridangam player is Karaikudi R Mani.
    • Mani, who received instruction from renowned tutors, has developed a distinctive playing style characterised by high virtuosity and enticing sound quality.
  • Ghatam:
    • Ghatam, a huge, conical clay water pot used in India as a percussion instrument.
    • The ghatam lacks a membrane covering its mouth, unlike other Indian percussion instruments like the tabla and mridangam. Ujjwal Kumar, a ghatam player, has lofty goals for the common 'desi' musical instrument.
  • Alghoza
    • A bamboo-made stringed instrument is called an Alghoza.
    • It is a significant Rajasthani folk instrument.
    • A double-flute frequently played by the Alwar-based Meo community.

questions.question: 'Pankhida' songs are sung by peasants of _____ while working on the fields.
questions.questionHtml: 'Pankhida' songs are sung by peasants of _____ while working on the fields.
questions.solution: Pankhida is a traditional folk song form originating from Rajasthan, India, and is sung by peasants while working in the fields. The word 'Pankhida' translates to 'lover' in the local dialect. These songs are typically performed with traditional instruments such as the Algoza and the Manjira. They often follow a call-and-response format, with a lead singer performing a verse and the group responding with a chorus. Other folk music forms from different states include Sohar, Sumangali, and Ropnigeet from Bihar; Dalkhai, Karma, and Rangabati from Odisha; and Sohar, Kaharwa, and Chanayni from Uttar Pradesh.

questions.question: Jaggahalige Kunita, which includes the vachanas of Basavanna, is folk music from the Indian state of ______.
questions.questionHtml: Jaggahalige Kunita, which includes the vachanas of Basavanna, is folk music from the Indian state of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Karnataka.

Key Points

  • Jaggahalige Kunita
    • This is a folk art of the Hubballi Dharwad region (particularly the village of Byahatti), which is performed on occasions such as Ugadi and Holi.
    • The Jagghalige is a percussion instrument made from a bullock cart wheel wrapped in buffalo hide.
    • The villagers roll out the large instruments and march in procession.
    • The performance is directed by a choreographer playing a much-smaller percussion instrument called the Kanihaligi, made of clay and covered with calf hide.
    • The performance usually involves about 15 people.

Additional Information

  • Karadi Majalu
    • This is a popular group of folk music in north Karnataka, performed during occasions and in processions.
    • The Karadi or Karade is the percussion instrument used by the group.
    • It is a palm-sized cymbal producing metallic sounds, and the shehnai produces the melody.
  • Krishna Parijatha
    • Krishna Parijatha is a theatre popular in North Karnataka.
    • It is a combination of Yakshagana and Bayalata, portraying stories or scenes from the Mahabharata

questions.question: Which of the following instruments is played by P Mani Iyer?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following instruments is played by P Mani Iyer?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Mridangam.

Key Points

  • P Mani Iyer
    • Palghat T. S. Mani Iyer, born Thiruvilvamalai Ramaswamy was one of the leading mridangists in the field of Carnatic music.
    • He, along with his contemporaries Palani Subramaniam Pillai and Ramanathapuram C.S. Murugabhoopathy, are revered as the "Holy Trinity of Mrudangam".
    • Mani Iyer was the first mridangist to be awarded the Sangeetha Kalanidhi presented by the Music Academy of Madras, the Padma Bhushan and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Awards presented by the Government of India.
    • Mani Iyer accompanied all the leading vocal artists of his era.
    • He was also the guru for later mridangam players such as Late Palghat R. Raghu, Late Mavelikkara Velukkutty Nair, Umayalpuram K. Sivaraman, Thanjavur R.Ramadas, Kamalakar Rao, Late G. Harishankar (kanjira),etc.

Additional Information

  •  mridangam
    • The mridangam is a percussion instrument of ancient origin.
    • It is the primary rhythmic accompaniment in a Carnatic music ensemble.
  •  sarangi
    • The sarangi is a bowed, short-necked string instrument played in traditional music from India – Punjabi folk music, Rajasthani folk music, and Boro folk music – also in Pakistan and Bangladesh.
  • violin
    • The violin, sometimes known as a fiddle, is a wooden chordophone in the violin family.
    • Most violins have a hollow mandolin.
    • It is the smallest and thus highest-pitched instrument in the family in regular use.
  • mandolin
    • A mandolin is a stringed musical instrument in the lute family and is generally plucked with a plectrum

questions.question: Brij Bhushan Kabra was considered an expert in which of the following instruments in the field of Indian classical music?
questions.questionHtml: Brij Bhushan Kabra was considered an expert in which of the following instruments in the field of Indian classical music?
questions.solution: Brij Bhushan Kabra was a distinguished Indian classical musician renowned for his expertise in the guitar. He introduced the guitar to Indian classical music, adapting it to the Hindustani tradition. Kabra's innovative approach popularized the guitar in this genre, inspiring many musicians. Born in Jodhpur, Rajasthan, he initially trained in vocal music before switching to the guitar, influenced by sitar maestro Pt. Ravi Shankar. His landmark album "Call of the Valley" with Pt. Shivkumar Sharma and Pt. Hariprasad Chaurasia is highly celebrated. Kabra's contributions have earned him significant recognition and accolades in music.

questions.question: Who among the following was the son of Ustad Allauddin Khan?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following was the son of Ustad Allauddin Khan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Ali Akbar KhanKey Points

  •  Ali Akbar Khan was the son of Ustad Allauddin Khan: 
  • Ali Akbar Khan was a Hindustani classical musician who played the sarod.
  • He was a member of the Maihar gharana and was known for his virtuosity.
  • He was awarded the Padma Bhushan in 1967 and the Padma Vibhushan in 1989.

questions.question: Bickram Ghosh, a recipient of Global Indian Music Award, is a music composer and an Indian classical _______ player.
questions.questionHtml: Bickram Ghosh, a recipient of Global Indian Music Award, is a music composer and an Indian classical _______ player.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is tabla.

Key PointsBickram Ghosh

  • Bickram Ghosh is an Indian classical tabla player.
  • He started learning tabla from his father, Pandit Shankar Ghosh.
  • He has performed with Ali Akbar Khan and Pandit Ravi Shankar.
  • He launched his music company, Melting Pot Productions, in October 2010.
  • On 1 October 2012, he won the 2012 Global Indian Music Academy (GIMA) Awards for his composition Vande Mataram.
  • In June 2012, he performed a concert "One World Fusion Extravaganza" at Shilpakala Vedika auditorium in Hyderabad.

Additional InformationTanpura

  • The tanpura or tambura, tanpuri is a long-necked plucked string instrument, originating from India.
  • It supports and sustains the melody of another instrument or singer by providing a continuous harmonic bourdon or drone. 
  • Hindustani musicians favor the term tanpura whereas Carnatic musicians say tambura.
  • Gowrishankar Gurusawmy, Soman Pillai, Prasanna Athele are some of the famous tambura players.

Sarangi

  • Sarangi, also called saran or saranga is a short-necked fiddle used throughout South Asia.
  • It measures about 76 cm (30 inches) long.
  • The instrument has a roughly rectangular slightly waisted body and broad fretless neck.
  • It has three melody strings made of gut.

Bansuri

  • A bansuri is an ancient side-blown flute originating from the Indian subcontinent.
  • It is an aerophone produced from bamboo, and used in Hindustani classical music.
  • It is referred to as nadi and tunava in the Rigveda and other Vedic texts of Hinduism.
  • Its importance and operation are discussed in the Sanskrit text Natya Shastra.
  • Bansuri is traditionally made from a single hollow shaft of bamboo with six or seven finger holes.
  • Some modern designs come in ivory, fiberglass, and various metals.

questions.question: Who among the following Hindustani classical musicians was NOT associated with ‘Maihar Gharana’?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following Hindustani classical musicians was NOT associated with ‘Maihar Gharana’?
questions.solution: Ustad Bismillah Khan, a legendary shehnai player, was not associated with the Maihar Gharana. He belonged to the Benares Gharana and was deeply rooted in the traditional folk and classical music of Benares (Varanasi). His work was central to the Ganga-Jamuni tehzeeb (syncretic culture) of the region. In contrast, Ali Akbar Khan (sarod player), Pt Ravi Shankar (sitar player), and Annapurna Devi (surbahar player) were all key figures associated with the Maihar Gharana, each contributing significantly to its development and popularity.

questions.question: Posthumus Padma awardee in 2022, Gosaveedu Shalik Hassan was a renowned player of the _________.
questions.questionHtml: Posthumus Padma awardee in 2022, Gosaveedu Shalik Hassan was a renowned player of the _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Nadaswaram.

Key Points

  • Gosaveedu Shalik Hassan was a celebrated player of the Nadaswaram, a traditional Indian musical instrument.
  • He was posthumously awarded the Padma Shri in 2022 for his contributions to Indian classical music.
  • Nadaswaram is a wind instrument, often referred to as the world's loudest non-brass acoustic instrument.
  • It is commonly played in South Indian classical music, especially during temple festivals and weddings.

Additional Information

  • Padma Awards
    • Padma Awards are one of the highest civilian honors in India, instituted in the year 1954.
    • They are given in three categories: Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan, and Padma Shri, in decreasing order of precedence.
    • The awards are given in various disciplines/fields of activities, including art, social work, public affairs, science and engineering, trade and industry, medicine, literature and education, sports, and civil service.
  • Indian Classical Music
    • Indian classical music is divided into two major traditions: Hindustani (North Indian) and Carnatic (South Indian).
    • Nadaswaram is predominantly used in Carnatic music.
    • It is often accompanied by another instrument called "Thavil", a type of drum.
  • Traditional Indian Instruments
    • India has a rich tradition of music with a variety of instruments like Sitar, Veena, Tabla, Mridangam, and more.
    • Each instrument has its unique sound and playing technique, deeply rooted in the cultural and religious practices of the region.

questions.question: How many basic talams are there in Indian Classical Carnatic music?
questions.questionHtml: How many basic talams are there in Indian Classical Carnatic music?
questions.solution: In Indian Classical Carnatic music, there are 7 basic talams: Dhruva, Matya, Rupaka, Jhampa, Triputa, Ata, and Eka. Each talam has a unique structure that maintains rhythm in compositions. These basic talams can be expanded into 35 talams by applying five jatis (types of rhythmic units). Talam is crucial in Carnatic music, providing the rhythmic framework for performances.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT related to the ‘Trinity of Carnatic Music’?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is NOT related to the ‘Trinity of Carnatic Music’?
questions.solution: The 'Trinity of Carnatic Music' consists of Syama Shastri, Tyagaraja, and Muthuswami Dikshitar, who are revered composers and foundational figures in Carnatic music. Their compositions, known for intricate melodies and deep devotion, form a crucial part of the Carnatic repertoire. They were contemporaries living between the late 18th and early 19th centuries. Purandara Das, although a significant figure and often called the "father of Carnatic music," is not part of this trinity. He lived earlier and is credited with systematizing Carnatic music teaching and composing numerous devotional songs.

questions.question: Mame Khan, an Indian folk singer known for his Sufi and folk music performances, is from the state of _________.
questions.questionHtml: Mame Khan, an Indian folk singer known for his Sufi and folk music performances, is from the state of _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Rajasthan.

Key Points

  • Mame Khan is a renowned Indian folk singer known for his mesmerizing Sufi and folk music performances.
  • He hails from the state of Rajasthan, which is known for its rich tradition of folk music.
  • Khan belongs to the Manganiyar community, a traditional musician caste from Rajasthan.
  • He has performed at various national and international platforms, bringing Rajasthani folk music to a global audience.
  • Khan's music often features traditional instruments like the khartal, dholak, and harmonium.

Additional Information

  • Rajasthani Folk Music
    • Rajasthani folk music is characterized by its distinct melodies and rhythms, often reflecting the region's history and culture.
    • It includes various forms such as Maand, Bhopa-Bhopi, and Panihari, each with its unique style and significance.
    • Instruments commonly used include the sarangi, kamayacha, and morchang.
    • This musical tradition is often passed down orally through generations within specific communities.
  • Manganiyar Community
    • The Manganiyars are a community of hereditary musicians in Rajasthan and parts of Sindh in Pakistan.
    • They traditionally serve as court musicians for Rajput patrons but also perform for various social and religious events.
    • Their music often includes themes of devotion, love, and historical tales.
    • The community has been instrumental in keeping the folk music traditions alive and vibrant.
  • Sufi Music
    • Sufi music is a genre of music inspired by Sufism, the mystical dimension of Islam.
    • It aims to induce a state of spiritual trance and is often performed during Sufi gatherings and festivals.
    • Instruments like the tabla, harmonium, and sitar are commonly used in Sufi music.
    • Prominent forms include Qawwali and Ghazal, which have found a significant place in South Asian music culture.
  • Global Recognition
    • Rajasthani folk music, including the performances by artists like Mame Khan, has gained international acclaim.
    • These artists have performed at prestigious festivals and events around the world, promoting cultural exchange.
    • Efforts by the government and cultural organizations have helped in preserving and promoting this rich heritage.
    • Documentaries and music albums featuring Rajasthani folk music have contributed to its global popularity.

questions.question: The important singers of ___________Gharana are Faiyyaz Khan, Latafat Hussein Khan and Dinkar Kakini.
questions.questionHtml: The important singers of ___________Gharana are Faiyyaz Khan, Latafat Hussein Khan and Dinkar Kakini.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Agra Gharana.

Key Points

  • The Agra Gharana places great importance on developing forcefulness and deepness in the voice so that the notes are powerful and resonant. Exponents -The important singers of this Gharana are Faiyyaz Khan, Latafat Hussein Khan, and Dinkar Kakini.
  • The Agra gharana is a tradition of Hindustani classical vocal music descended from the Nauhar Bani.
  • So far, Nauhar Bani has been traced back to around 1300 AD, during the reign of Emperor Allauddin Khilji of Delhi.
  • The first known musician of this tradition is Nayak Gopal.
  • Agra Gharana is a blend of Khayal Gayaki and Dhrupad-Dhamar.
  • The music of Agra Gharana finds its place in almost all the important musical functions throughout the country. 

Additional Information

  • The Patiala gharana is one of the vocal gharanas of Hindustani classical music, named after the city of Patiala in Punjab, India.
  • The Mewati gharana is a musical apprenticeship tribe of Hindustani classical music. Known for being Pandit Jasraj's musical lineage, the gharana was founded by brothers Utd. Ghagge Nazir Khan and Utd. Wahid Khan of Indore in the late 19th century at the Holkar Court.
  • The Benares gharana is one of the six most common styles of playing the Indian tabla.

questions.question: Lalitha and Saroja Chidambaram are the noted _______ singers.
questions.questionHtml: Lalitha and Saroja Chidambaram are the noted _______ singers.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Carnatic.

Key Points

  • Lalitha and Saroja Chidambaram are renowned for their contributions to Carnatic music, a classical music form of South India.
  • Carnatic music is known for its intricate rhythms and devotion to melody, often focusing on compositions known as kritis.
  • The Chidambaram sisters have performed in many prestigious music festivals and have been honored with numerous awards for their musical excellence.
  • Carnatic music is typically performed with vocalists accompanied by instrumentalists, including the violin, mridangam, and veena.

Additional Information

  • Folk Music
    • Folk music is a genre that reflects the traditional music of a community or region.
    • It is often passed down orally through generations and can vary widely from one culture to another.
    • Examples include bhangra from Punjab, Baul songs from Bengal, and Lavani from Maharashtra.
  • Sufi Music
    • Sufi music is associated with the mystical branch of Islam known as Sufism.
    • It often includes devotional songs known as qawwalis, which aim to inspire spiritual growth and connection with the divine.
    • Famous Sufi musicians include Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan and Abida Parveen.
  • Hindustani Classical Music
    • Hindustani classical music is a major tradition of Indian classical music, prevalent in North India.
    • It is characterized by its elaborate ragas (melodic frameworks) and talas (rhythmic cycles).
    • Prominent exponents include Ravi Shankar, Zakir Hussain, and Bhimsen Joshi.
  • Carnatic Music
    • Carnatic music is the classical music tradition of South India.
    • It emphasizes vocal music, with compositions known as kritis forming the core of the repertoire.
    • It is known for its complex rhythms (tala) and melodic patterns (raga).
    • Famous Carnatic musicians include M. S. Subbulakshmi, Tyagaraja, and M. Balamuralikrishna.

questions.question: For which of the following tribal music and dance forms was Arjun Singh Dhurve conferred with Tulsi Samman?
questions.questionHtml: For which of the following tribal music and dance forms was Arjun Singh Dhurve conferred with Tulsi Samman?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Baiga.

Key Points

  • Arjun Singh Dhurve was honored with the Tulsi Samman for his exceptional contribution to the Baiga tribal music and dance form.
  • The Baiga tribe is one of the prominent tribes in Madhya Pradesh, India, known for its vibrant culture and traditional practices.
  • The Baiga dance is an integral part of their customs, often performed during festivals and important community events.
  • The Tulsi Samman is a prestigious award given by the Madhya Pradesh government to individuals who have made significant contributions in the field of tribal art and culture.

Additional Information

  • Tribal Music and Dance Forms
    • Mardana: This is a traditional form of music and dance practiced by the tribal communities in various regions of India. It involves the use of traditional instruments and vibrant costumes.
    • Pawara: A tribal dance form from the Pawara community, known for its rhythmic movements and cultural significance. It is usually performed during festivals and special occasions.
    • Baiga: The Baiga tribe's dance form, which Arjun Singh Dhurve is recognized for, is characterized by its unique steps, rhythmic beats, and cultural expressions. The dancers often wear traditional attire made from natural materials.
    • Jhumta: A traditional dance form performed by various tribal communities, often during harvest seasons and festivals. It involves group formations and synchronized movements.
  • Tulsi Samman
    • The Tulsi Samman is an award given by the Madhya Pradesh government to recognize and honor individuals who have made outstanding contributions to tribal art and culture.
    • It aims to preserve and promote the rich cultural heritage of the tribal communities in the region.
    • The award is named after the renowned poet and saint, Tulsidas, and is a symbol of cultural pride and recognition.
